responseText:
I can’t access or change your mailbox directly. I can, however, give exact steps you can use to find and remove all Uber messages and optionally stop them from coming in.

Important: double-check messages before deleting (receipts, account/security emails). If you accidentally delete something, Gmail Trash keeps it 30 days.

If you use Gmail (web)
1. Search and review
   - In the search box try: uber
   - Or more restrictive: from:(@uber.com) OR from:(uber)
   - Review results to confirm these are the messages you want removed.

2. Bulk delete
   - Click the checkbox in the top-left to select visible conversations.
   - Click the link that appears: “Select all conversations that match this search.”
   - Click the trash icon to delete all selected conversations. They go to Trash for 30 days.

3. Create a filter to auto-delete future Uber messages
   - Click the search options icon (sliders) in the search box.
   - In “From” enter: uber
   - Click “Create filter”.
   - Check “Delete it” (or “Skip the Inbox (Archive it)” if you prefer to keep them but out of your inbox).
   - Optionally check “Also apply filter to matching conversations.”
   - Click “Create filter”.

4. Block or mark as spam (alternative)
   - Open an Uber message, click the three-dot menu, choose “Block [sender]” or “Report spam” (spam moves messages automatically to Spam).

If you use Gmail app (Android/iOS)
- Search for “uber”, tap the profile icons to select messages, then tap the trash icon to delete.
- To block or report: open a message, tap the three-dot menu and choose “Block” or “Report spam”.
- To create filters you’ll need to use Gmail on the web (desktop).

If you use Outlook, Apple Mail, or another provider
- Use their search for “uber” to find messages, select and delete in bulk.
- Create a Rule/Filter (e.g., From contains “uber”) to auto-delete or move to a folder.

Want help?
- Tell me which email provider you use (Gmail, Outlook, etc.) and whether you want messages automatically deleted or just archived. I can give the exact search string and step-by-step tailored to that provider.
